PullRequest.Title: plugins: refactor pluginSources with proper deletion
PullRequest.Body:
- Consolidate source logic into IPluginSource implementations
- Use that to implement more robust cleanup logic

Closes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297251

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each uninstall discarded the only installed-plugin reference while leaving the cloned repository or npm/pip package tree on disk indefinitely. Repeated install/uninstall cycles, especially across distinct direct-source plugins, therefore accumulated filesystem bytes and directory entries without a lifecycle cleanup path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Agent plugin cache disk usage grew monotonically across uninstall cycles, with later cache scans and filesystem maintenance operating over retained plugin trees.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Uninstall still removes plugin metadata immediately, then asynchronously resolves and recursively deletes the direct source's cache directory and prunes empty parents. Relative marketplace paths remain untouched because they share a repository cache.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery's remove callback only called removeInstalledPlugin(entry.pluginUri), which removes the persisted metadata entry. Direct GitHub/Git URL/npm/pip installs place cloned repositories or package trees under cacheHome/agentPlugins, and no other base-revision removal path deletes those source-owned directories. The PR adds cleanupPluginSource at RIGHT line 917; getCleanupTarget identifies the source-owned cache directory and cleanupPluginSource recursively deletes it after uninstall.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent plugin service startup and installed-plugin discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating IAgentPluginService starts MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery, reads the installed-plugin memento, and sequentially resolves each installed plugin directory before publishing the plugin list. The new repository-service injection is on this path, but PluginMarketplaceService already depended on that service before the diff. Constructing the five source strategy objects performs no filesystem, subprocess, IPC, or network work; delayed service dependencies such as ITerminalService remain proxies until accessed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each persisted installed plugin URI and detect plugin format files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory resolve per installed plugin, plus existing format-detection probes for each distinct URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same installed-plugin discovery loop and per-plugin filesystem reads ran before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These reads must complete before the discovered marketplace plugin list is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persisted installed plugins; effective cardinality is one source per distinct plugin URI after existing deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Installed plugin filesystem resolves are serialized by the existing for/await loop. The diff adds no queue, fan-out, or new parallel work on startup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed plugin metadata comes from the existing application-scoped memento. Source strategies hold no new cache contents; the terminal service remains delayed. Cold and warm discovery retain the existing per-installed-plugin filesystem probes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor dependencies, delayed singleton registration, strategy constructors, and the discovery loop were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of installed plugins varies, but the diff does not alter that cardinality or the existing serialized reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added strategy instances are lightweight and introduce no expensive startup boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install or update a GitHub/Git URL/relative-path plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user install/update awaits the existing filesystem existence check and Git command sequence. Cold direct-source install creates the parent and clones once, then optionally checks out a revision; warm ensure skips cloning and only checks out a requested revision. Relative-path update still delegates to pullRepository through the new strategy dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the direct-source repository exists and create its parent on a cold install.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists call per install/ensure; one createFolder only on a cold cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same exists/createFolder operations were previously implemented directly in AgentPluginRepositoryService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existence check selects the cold clone or warm reuse path and is awaited by installation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone, pull/fetch, and optionally check out the Git repository through Git commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold install performs one clone and at most one checkout; update performs one pull or fetch and at most one checkout for the single selected plugin/source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command sequence and cache keying existed before the strategy extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Git commands must finish before install/update completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin and one source repository per action; no collection scaling after cache lookup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One sequential Git operation chain per user action. The diff neither adds aggregate fan-out nor changes the absence of a cross-action limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cache keys remain source URL/repository plus ref or SHA. A warm direct-source cache avoids clone; relative-path plugins continue sharing the marketplace repository cache. There is no negative cache or newly defeated coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: old and new implementations show equivalent filesystem and Git command sequences.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size and Git latency vary, but operation count and placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The source-strategy refactor preserves cold/warm Git boundary counts and critical-path ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install or update an npm/pip plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After confirmation, the action creates/uses the package cache directory, launches one terminal-backed npm or pip install, waits for command completion, and checks the resulting plugin path before registering it. The newly explicit createFolder occurs before confirmation via ensurePluginSource, but it is one bounded filesystem operation per action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the package cache directory and check for the installed package path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One createFolder and one post-install exists check per confirmed install path; repeated calls target the same package-keyed directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old package ensure path only computed the cache URI, while the package manager created its prefix/target. The additional idempotent createFolder is a single bounded call, not realistic enough to constitute a performance regression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: createFolder precedes the confirmation/terminal command and exists validation follows it; both are awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one npm install or pip install command in a transient terminal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one package-manager command per user install/update after confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: PluginInstallService previously ran the same one terminal command with equivalent arguments and completion waiting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Command completion is the dominant awaited installation work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected package per action; no per-dependency application-level fan-out beyond work internal to npm/pip.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One terminal command is awaited per action. Rapid independent user actions can still overlap, as before; the diff introduces no collection-driven burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Package cache keys remain sanitized package names; warm installs reuse the same prefix/target but intentionally rerun the package manager on update. Failed/cancelled attempts are not negatively cached, matching prior behavior aside from an empty directory possibly being created.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: argument building, terminal execution, and post-install validation were moved nearly verbatim.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Package size and package-manager duration vary widely, but the expensive subprocess count is unchanged and the one added createFolder is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional idempotent directory creation is minor relative to the unchanged package-manager command and does not scale across a collection.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI removes persisted metadata synchronously, then starts cleanup without awaiting it, so recursive cache deletion is off the uninstall UI critical path. Cleanup checks for one source-owned directory, recursively deletes it, then walks only its ancestor depth toward the cache root while parents remain empty.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check for and recursively delete the direct source cache, then resolve/delete empty ancestor directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists call and at most one recursive subtree delete per uninstalled direct-source plugin, followed by O(path depth) parent resolve/delete calls; relative-path plugins perform none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, uninstall removed only metadata and retained Git/package cache trees indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The work is fire-and-forget after metadata removal and does not delay the uninstall action or plugin-list refresh.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size of the selected plugin cache subtree and URI ancestor depth; across actions, the number of explicitly uninstalled direct-source plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One cleanup task is launched per uninstall. Separate rapid uninstalls may overlap because there is no shared limiter, but ordinary UI actions are individual and each task owns one cache subtree; no realistic catastrophic burst was established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Git cache keys remain repository/URL plus revision; npm/pip keys remain package based. Cleanup invalidates exactly the selected direct-source key and skips shared relative marketplace repositories. There is no warm reuse after intentional uninstall.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the remove callback, cleanup target rules, recursive delete, and bounded parent walk were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cache subtree sizes and frequency of bulk rapid uninstalls vary, but each deletion is tied to a user-selected plugin and is off the immediate UI critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression finding. This is intentional lifecycle cleanup that removes previously retained filesystem data; the prior retention was recorded as a regression fix.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and every patch. Install/update boundary counts are preserved by the strategy extraction, startup adds only lightweight strategy objects with delayed service proxies, and uninstall introduces one off-critical-path cache deletion per direct-source plugin. No actionable performance regression was found; the concrete fix for indefinitely retained direct-source caches was recorded with its introducing commit.
